edges.description: Mechanical and chemical activation of nociceptor terminals in the injured tissue releases the neuropeptides that produce the local inflammatory response.
How local neuro-immune activation breaks tolerance to autonomic receptor epitopes is not established; the edge is recorded at that strength.
Sustained nociceptive input from the inflamed limb drives the spinal changes curated downstream.
The transition from the early vasodilated limb to the later cold, cyanotic one accompanies the inflammatory response, but the mechanism of the switch is not resolved.
Local inflammatory cytokines are the proposed route to the periarticular bone loss that three-phase scintigraphy detects.

Patient IgG transferred to incised mice produces sustained microglial and astrocyte activation in the dorsal horn and pain-related brain regions, with microglia-derived IL-1beta as a demonstrated intermediate.
The antibodies are agonist-like at receptors on autonomic neurons, so their action on vasomotor control is direct rather than mediated.
Activated glia release IL-1beta and other mediators into the dorsal horn, lowering the threshold for nociceptive transmission — the step the IL-1 rescue experiment isolates.
Persistent altered afferent input is the presumed driver of the cortical map change; the intermediates are not established, and the direction of causation between the two is itself an open question.
The fracture is the tissue trauma node; the link makes the disease-level exposure explicit in the pathograph rather than leaving it implied.

edges.description: Reproduces the sustained microglial and astrocyte activation in the dorsal horn and pain-related brain regions that defines this node, driven by the human patient-derived agent rather than by a synthetic surrogate.
edges.limitations: The donor IgG comes from patients with longstanding CRPS, so the model speaks to maintenance rather than initiation; the recipients are female C57BL/6 mice with a surgical incision rather than a fracture; and the hyperalgesia readout does not capture the vasomotor, sudomotor, and trophic domains that make up three quarters of the human criteria set.

edges.description: The model does not reproduce autoantibody production — it supplies the antibodies directly, which is precisely what isolates their contribution from everything else in the patient.
edges.limitations: Because the antibodies are administered rather than generated, the model is silent on how tolerance is broken in patients, which remains unexplained.
edges.source: CRPS IgG passive transfer into incised mice

edges.description: Reproduces the inflammatory and trophic features of early CRPS — oedema, warmth, skin thickening, osteoporosis — together with the neuropeptide and cytokine changes that this node's mechanism predicts.
edges.limitations: The recapitulation is of early CRPS only. Most post-fracture changes resolve within roughly five months, so the model does not capture whatever converts an acute post-traumatic response into the chronic syndrome, and the review that summarizes it notes significant differences from the human literature alongside the correspondences.
edges.source: Rodent tibia fracture and cast immobilization model

edges.description: Tibia fracture alone activates spinal glia and upregulates spinal neuropeptide, cytokine and NGF expression — the same central response the IgG transfer model produces, reached from the peripheral injury instead.
edges.limitations: The review reports the central changes qualitatively in aggregate across studies rather than as one controlled measurement, and the same five-month resolution caveat applies.
edges.source: Rodent tibia fracture and cast immobilization model

nodes.description: Functionally active IgG directed at the second extracellular loop of the beta-2 adrenergic and muscarinic-2 receptors, with agonist-like properties in a cardiomyocyte bioassay. These are not bystander antibodies: they act on the receptors, they are found in a defined subset of patients, and their transfer into injured mice reproduces the syndrome. The node is the hinge of the entry — it converts a post-traumatic inflammatory response into a self-sustaining one.

animal_models.description: The model does not reproduce autoantibody production — it supplies the antibodies directly, which is precisely what isolates their contribution from everything else in the patient.
animal_models.genotype: Female C57BL/6 with plantar skin-muscle incision, treated with purified IgG from patients with longstanding CRPS
animal_models.name: CRPS IgG passive transfer into incised mice

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmunity against the β2 adrenergic receptor and muscarinic-2 receptor in complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We identified these autoantibodies as immunoglobulin G directed against peptide sequences from the second extracellular loop of these receptors.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmunity against the β2 adrenergic receptor and muscarinic-2 receptor in complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The identification of functionally active autoantibodies in serum samples from CRPS patients supports an autoimmune pathogenesis of CRPS.

evidence.reference_title: The prevalence of autoantibodies in complex regional pain syndrome type I.
evidence.snippet: Twenty seven (33%) of the 82 CRPS patients of whom serum was available showed a positive ANA test. This prevalence is significantly higher than in the general population.

nodes.description: The model that makes the autoimmune arm causal. Purified IgG from patients with longstanding CRPS, given daily to mice with a small plantar incision, produces prolonged swelling and stable hyperalgesia and sustained central glial activation relative to healthy-control IgG. The design is what earns the weight: a human-derived agent, a healthy-donor control arm, a mechanistic knockout, a pharmacological block, and a treatment arm started after the phenotype was established.
nodes.id: CRPS IgG passive transfer into incised mice

evidence.reference_title: Transfer of complex regional pain syndrome to mice via human autoantibodies is mediated by interleukin-1-induced mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: These results indicate that persistent CRPS is often contributed to by autoantibodies and highlight a potential therapeutic use for clinically licensed antagonists, such as anakinra, to prevent or treat CRPS via blocking IL-1 actions.

nodes.description: An NMDA-receptor-dependent lowering of the threshold for nociceptive transmission, so that innocuous input is experienced as painful and painful input as more so, over a territory well beyond the original injury. It is the state that allodynia and hyperalgesia report, and the node ketamine targets: the NMDA receptor is the reason a dissociative anaesthetic has an analgesic role in this disease at all.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms of complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Key mechanisms underlying clinical manifestations include peripheral and central sensitization, sympathetic dysregulation, and alterations in somatosensory processing.

evidence.reference_title: Outpatient intravenous ketamine for the treatment of complex regional pain syndrome: a double-blind placebo controlled study.
evidence.snippet: The pathophysiology of CRPS is not known but both clinical and experimental evidence demonstrate the important of the NMDA receptor and glial activation in its induction and maintenance.

nodes.description: The cortical representation of the affected hand in primary somatosensory cortex shrinks and its centre shifts toward the lip representation, while tactile-evoked S1 responses on the affected side are increased. The extent of reorganization correlates with pain and, more strongly, with mechanical hyperalgesia, and mechanical hyperalgesia is its best single predictor. This node is the target of the rehabilitative treatments — graded motor imagery and mirror therapy — that work by restoring coherent sensorimotor representation rather than by any pharmacological action.

evidence.reference_title: Patterns of cortical reorganization in complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The center of the hand was shifted toward the cortical representation of the lip.

evidence.reference_title: Patterns of cortical reorganization in complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Using multiple regression analysis, the best predictor for the plastic changes was found to be mechanical hyperalgesia.

nodes.description: The commonest inciting event. Fracture accounted for 46% of triggers in the Olmsted County series, and distal radius fracture is the classic setting — which is also why the disease has a genuine primary-prevention option, since that population is identifiable at the moment of injury.

evidence.reference_title: Complex regional pain syndrome type I: incidence and prevalence in Olmsted county, a population-based study.
evidence.snippet: All cases reported an antecedent event and fracture was the most common trigger (46%).

nodes.description: A sequenced rehabilitative program — limb laterality recognition, then explicit motor imagery, then mirror therapy — aimed at the cortical representation rather than at any peripheral target. It is curated with its evidence caveat: a systematic review supports an effect on pain and function, but the trial base is small and heterogeneous.
nodes.id: Graded motor imagery and mirror therapy

evidence.reference_title: Update on the effects of graded motor imagery and mirror therapy on complex regional pain syndrome type 1: A systematic review.
evidence.snippet: GMI and MT can improve pain in patients with CRPS type 1; however, there is not sufficient evidence to recommend these therapies over other treatments given the small size and heterogeneity of the studied population.

nodes.description: An NMDA-receptor antagonist, and the treatment that targets the central sensitization node directly. In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, four-hour daily outpatient infusions for ten days produced statistically significant reductions in many pain parameters, with the placebo group showing no treatment effect in any parameter. The trial is small and its authors call explicitly for a larger one with higher doses and longer follow-up, and a 2025 systematic review characterizes the analgesia as strong but short-term with no long-term data — so this is curated as an evidenced treatment with an explicitly bounded claim.

evidence.reference_title: Outpatient intravenous ketamine for the treatment of complex regional pain syndrome: a double-blind placebo controlled study.
evidence.snippet: This study showed that intravenous ketamine administered in an outpatient setting resulted in statistically significant (p<0.05) reductions in many pain parameters. It also showed that subjects in our placebo group demonstrated no treatment effect in any parameter.

evidence.reference_title: The Analgesic Efficacy of Therapies Used for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: Intravenous ketamine demonstrated strong short-term analgesia, though findings were limited by small samples, variable protocols, and lack of long-term data.

nodes.description: An amino-bisphosphonate, and the intervention with the strongest randomized evidence in CRPS-I. In a multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 82 patients, four 100 mg infusions over ten days produced a substantially greater fall in visual analogue pain score than placebo, with the effect sustained, replicated in the open-label crossover of the former placebo group, and with no patient reporting CRPS-related symptoms a year later.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of complex regional pain syndrome type I with neridronate: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
evidence.snippet: In patients with acute CRPS-I, four i.v. infusions of neridronate 100 mg are associated with clinically relevant and persistent benefits.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of complex regional pain syndrome type I with neridronate: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
evidence.snippet: During the open-extension phase in the formerly placebo group the results of treatment were superimposable on those seen during the blind phase in the active group.

nodes.description: Activated C-fibre nociceptors release substance P and CGRP into the injured limb, producing vasodilation, plasma extravasation, oedema, erythema, and increased sweating, and recruiting local immune cells. This node is the direct substrate of three of the four Budapest domains — vasomotor, sudomotor/oedema, and part of the trophic — and it is what makes early CRPS a warm, swollen limb rather than a purely sensory complaint.

animal_models.description: Reproduces the inflammatory and trophic features of early CRPS — oedema, warmth, skin thickening, osteoporosis — together with the neuropeptide and cytokine changes that this node's mechanism predicts.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features and pathophysiology of complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Compelling evidence implicates biological pathways that underlie aberrant inflammation, vasomotor dysfunction, and maladaptive neuroplasticity in the clinical features of CRPS.

nodes.description: The initiating event, and almost always a common one — distal limb fracture above all, with sprain, crush, surgery, and immobilization also recognized. In the Olmsted County population study every identified case reported an antecedent event and fracture was the trigger in 46%. Because the trigger is ubiquitous and the syndrome is rare, this node is necessary but far from sufficient, which is the premise of the whole entry.

evidence.reference_title: Complex regional pain syndrome type I: incidence and prevalence in Olmsted county, a population-based study.
evidence.snippet: All cases reported an antecedent event and fracture was the most common trigger (46%).

nodes.description: Patchy periarticular demineralization of the affected region — the finding Sudeck originally described as acute inflammatory bone atrophy, and the structural correlate of the intense periarticular uptake on the delayed phase of three-phase bone scintigraphy. It is curated as a distinct node because it is the target of the treatment with the strongest randomized evidence in this disease: intravenous bisphosphonate.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms of complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The primary pathology of both types of CRPS (Type I, also known as reflex sympathetic dystrophy, RSD; Type II, also known as causalgia) is featured by allodynia, edema, changes in skin color and temperature, and dystrophy, predominantly affecting extremities.

nodes.description: The model built to match the commonest human trigger. Closed tibial fracture with casting reproduces the early syndrome broadly — spontaneous and evoked pain behaviour, warmth and oedema, skin thickening and osteoporosis — and has been the vehicle for much of the mechanistic work on neuropeptides, keratinocyte-derived cytokines and nerve growth factor, spinal glial activation, and the B-cell/IgM contribution. Its limitation is temporal and is the reason it is curated as partial: most post-fracture changes resolve within about five months, so the model may not contain whatever perpetuates chronic human CRPS.
nodes.id: Rodent tibia fracture and cast immobilization model

evidence.reference_title: The Rodent Tibia Fracture Model: A Critical Review and Comparison With the Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Literature.
evidence.snippet: Distal limb fracture is the most common cause of complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS), thus the rodent tibia fracture model (TFM) was developed to study CRPS pathogenesis.

nodes.description: Microglia and astrocytes in the dorsal horn and in pain-related brain regions become and remain activated. The passive transfer experiment shows this state persisting long after the peripheral inflammatory response has resolved, and identifies microglia-derived IL-1beta as the mediator — with IL-1 receptor blockade both preventing it and reversing an already established phenotype. It is curated separately from the sensitization it produces because the two have different drug targets: IL-1 blockade acts here, NMDA antagonism acts downstream.

evidence.reference_title: Transfer of complex regional pain syndrome to mice via human autoantibodies is mediated by interleukin-1-induced mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: After a short-lasting paw inflammatory response in all groups, CRPS IgG-injected mice displayed sustained, profound microglia and astrocyte activation in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord and pain-related brain regions, indicating central sensitization.

evidence.reference_title: Transfer of complex regional pain syndrome to mice via human autoantibodies is mediated by interleukin-1-induced mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, with the generation of an IL-1β floxed(fl/fl) mouse line, we demonstrated that CRPS IgG-induced changes are in part mediated by microglia-derived IL-1β, suggesting that both peripheral and central inflammatory mechanisms contribute to the transferred disease phenotype.

nodes.description: Disturbed sympathetic vasomotor control of the affected limb, producing the temperature and colour asymmetry of the vasomotor Budapest domain: an early warm, vasodilated phase and a later cold, cyanotic one. Importantly, not all CRPS pain is sympathetically maintained — a subset is sympathetically independent — which is the clearest explanation for why sympathetic blockade helps some patients and not others, and why this entry does not curate sympathetic block as a general treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms of complex regional pain syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Key mechanisms underlying clinical manifestations include peripheral and central sensitization, sympathetic dysregulation, and alterations in somatosensory processing.

nodes.description: The prevention arm, and the reason CRPS is unusual among chronic pain syndromes: a cheap supplement given after the commonest inciting injury lowers incidence. In a randomized multicentre dose-response trial of 416 patients with 427 wrist fractures, vitamin C reduced CRPS-I compared with placebo (2.4% vs 10.1%), with no further benefit at 1500 mg.
nodes.id: Vitamin C prophylaxis after wrist fracture

evidence.reference_title: Can vitamin C prevent complex regional pain syndrome in patients with wrist fractures? A randomized, controlled, multicenter dose-response study.
evidence.snippet: The prevalence of complex regional pain syndrome was 2.4% (eight of 328) in the vitamin C group and 10.1% (ten of ninety-nine) in the placebo group (p=0.002); all of the affected patients were elderly women.
